messages.content:
You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no physical body. Use their assigned canon constraints to choose permitted effects for the shared setting. Bodily wording about those subjects in the source is a metaphor, not permission to describe anatomy, hair, clothing, silhouettes or figures made of light in any look field. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. A seated metaphor permits an unoccupied seat and surrounding effects, not a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
The complete canon is supplied separately to rendering. Where constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects and leave their fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Describe only the effects needed for the section's shared setting or illumination, without enumerating all effects or copying fixed appearance into the look. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing remain valid look details. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return. People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor. Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.

STORY SECTION: The Ancient of Days and the son of man

- the_ancient_of_days: The Ancient of Days (hasForm: false)
- one_like_a_son_of_man: One like a son of man (hasForm: true)
- babylon: Babylon (hasForm: true)
- ministering_assembly_in_daniels_vision: Ministering assembly in Daniel's vision (hasForm: true)

NO-FORM CANON CONSTRAINTS (setting context; fixed descriptions are not section-look fields):
- the_ancient_of_days (stage: ancient-of-days-light): effect names for placement: radiance, fire, cloud, light
TEXT OF THE SECTION'S FIRST MOMENT (the look covers the whole section):
“I watched until thrones were placed, and one who was Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.

place.description: The shared physical place and surroundings. For a no-form subject's seated metaphor, describe an unoccupied seat and permitted surrounding effects, without bodily substitutes or fixed canon appearance. At most 200 characters.

timeOfDay.description: The time of day or change in time across the section, without a subject's fixed appearance. At most 200 characters.

weather.description: Shared environmental conditions, without bodily metaphors or fixed canon appearance. At most 200 characters.

light.description: Situational illumination shared by the section. Name a permitted no-form effect only where needed for the setting, leaving its fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials. At most 200 characters.

clothing.description: Only formed characters' situational clothing and shared props. Do not describe a no-form subject's clothing, hair, anatomy or garment substitutes, even as a denial. Leave fixed appearance to canon. At most 200 characters.

You are the scene planner of an illustration engine. You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, the section look, and the cast on stage in the section. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Choose which of the listed cast are present in this moment and name them in `present` by their ids; leave out cast who are elsewhere in the section. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that) and do not name an art style or rendering technique; describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
Presence does not require a physical body. A cast entry marked hasForm: false still belongs in the moment when represented through the non-figurative presence allowed by the brief and its supplied canon constraints. If you describe that entry's presence or action in any scene field, include its id in `present` so its canon constraints reach the image model. Select presence for this moment only; do not add cast who are absent or merely mentioned.
For each no-form subject, use its assigned canon to choose the permitted visible effects and their placement in the setting. Bodily wording about that subject in the source is a metaphor, not permission to give it a physical form. In every scene field, describe the permitted effects rather than bodily poses, anatomy, clothing, human silhouettes or figures made of light. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. When the source describes a no-form subject as seated, describe the unoccupied seat and the permitted surrounding effects rather than a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own poses, clothing and actions; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
Canon is supplied separately to rendering in full. When the constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects; their fixed appearance is deliberately omitted from this planning input. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Name only the permitted effect needed for this moment's placement or movement; leave its fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Do not enumerate all effects or copy the canon's descriptive qualifiers into any scene field. For example, given canon "The presence: brilliant gold radiance", plan "radiance spreading above the arch; the witness approaches". The plan contributes where the effect appears and what happens around it. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing still belong in the plan when the moment or look requires them; these are separate from the no-form subject's fixed appearance.

present.description: IDs of section cast present in this moment, including no-form subjects represented through their permitted effects. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or merely mentioned.

primarySubject.description: The main subject's placement or a formed character's situational pose. For a no-form subject, name the permitted effect and its position without its fixed colour, brightness or texture. For a seated metaphor, describe an unoccupied seat with effects around it. Example: radiance above an unoccupied seat; the witness looks up. At most 220 characters.

timeOfDay.description: This moment's time of day and situational illumination, consistent with the section look. Leave the no-form subject's fixed appearance in canon. At most 220 characters.

composition.description: Viewpoint, framing and relative placement of formed subjects, objects and permitted effects in one scene. Keep this independent of art style and rendering technique. At most 220 characters.
